summary: Uneven GPU share causing burst degradation and queue locks during short-stream flood
description:
Issue summary:
Customer is observing repeated p99 latency spikes and several batched request queue locks on their dedicated capacity cluster during short, high-concurrency bursts (many ~500–2,000 token short streams). Symptoms appear as back-to-back p99 degradations with worker queues hitting 'locked' state and a concurrent drop in aggregate throughput.

Impact:
- Customer-facing endpoints return elevated p50/p95/p99 (p99 up to 12s) for ~2–6 minute windows during short-stream flood events.
- Some requests return 504s if they hit a locked queue and fallback fails.
- Customer reports degraded product experience for interactive features during peak bursts.

Environment:
- Dedicated cluster: quanta-dedicated-prod-03 (customer: QuantaDocs Inc.)
- Region: us-west-2
- Serving runtime: 2026.02.2-nightly
- Autoscaler: autoscale-v1.7.3
- Scheduler: slot-allocator-v2

Steps to reproduce (observed in production):
1) Customer runs many concurrent short inference calls (avg 400 tokens) across 120 parallel clients for ~90s.
2) Platform schedules a mix of long-lived batched requests and many short streams which fragment available GPU slots.
3) Autoscaler attempts to react but scales in small increments due to burst smoothing policy.
4) Some GPU workers report 'queue lock' and stop accepting new batched work until eviction completes; requests are requeued causing head-of-line blocking.

Observed behavior (telemetry highlights):
- GPU slot utilization oscillates: some GPUs show 95% utilization while neighboring GPUs idle at ~20%.
- KV-cache growth spikes for the noisy tenant leading to increased memory residency on several workers.
- Autoscaler scale events lag the burst by ~60–90s; scale-up increments are insufficient to re-balance slot fragmentation.
- Logs show repeated 'batch_queue_lock' and 'slot_serialize_timeout' errors in serving-runtime.

Relevant logs and dashboards:
- Grafana dashboard (throughput/slots): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/slots/quanta-dedicated-prod-03
- Error logs (sample): https://logs.redwood.ai/q/abcd1234 (filter: batch_queue_lock)
- Slack incident channel: #support-quanta-flood (thread ts: 167/2039)

Hypothesis and initial findings:
- Primary hypothesis: Small-stream fanout from multiple clients (many short requests) causes slot fragmentation and uneven GPU slot allocation. The autoscaler smoothing policy and burst window cause delayed and under-sized scale-ups, which increases the chance of queue locks on already hot GPUs (noisy neighbor effect).
- Secondary: A specific tenant is producing KV-cache heavy requests that hold memory across batches, preventing efficient slot reuse on those GPUs.
- Observed that GPUs with heavy KV residency are more likely to hit 'slot_serialize_timeout' when a new batch attempts to use the same slot.

Actions taken so far:
- Support throttled the customer's concurrent client window by recommending a temporary rate limit at the API layer (applied for 15 minutes) — immediate improvement in p99 for the following burst.
- Eng on-call increased autoscaler aggressiveness for the dedicated pool as a mitigation (temporarily reduced burst smoothing from 30s to 10s).
- Placed a soft eviction on the KV-heavy tenant's long-lived KV caches to free memory on impacted workers (partial improvement).

Workarounds for customer:
- Spread requests across more logical routes to reduce per-route slot contention.
- Use client-side jittered backoff for short streams to avoid synchronized flooding.
- Pin low-latency routes to smaller batch sizes for interactive paths (reduces batching pressure).

Open questions / follow-ups required:
- Does the autoscaler math need to account for KV-cache memory residency in its scale decisions?
- Should we introduce preferential packing to avoid putting heavy-KV tenants on the same GPU as many short streams?
- Is there an opportunity to implement a fast-path bypass for very short streams to avoid batch serialization entirely?

Next steps (eng):
- SRE to collect a longer window of allocation traces for quanta-dedicated-prod-03 and run slot packing simulations (assigned INT ticket).
- Runtime team to triage 'slot_serialize_timeout' stack traces and add more granular logging for cache residency marks.
- Autoscaler team to evaluate a temporary policy tweak that allows a single, larger scale-up when fragmentation is detected.

Resolution note (tentative):
- Mitigations reduced recurrence frequency; full remediation requires changes across autoscaler and runtime packing. This ticket will track customer-facing mitigations and link to the internal remediation epic.
